item.title: C# Object to String Conversion: Direct Cast vs As Operator vs ToString()
item.description:
“C# Object to String Conversion: Direct Cast vs As Operator vs ToString()”

Evaluating Object Conversion Techniques in C#

The core debate revolves around safety, expected outcomes, and explicit vs. implicit type intentions.

1. Direct Casting: string s = (string)o;

This syntax demands that o must genuinely be convertible to a string at runtime.

  • Behavior: If o is indeed a string, the conversion succeeds, and the reference is assigned to s. If o is null, the assignment still occurs, setting s to null.
  • Failure Mode: If o is not null and not a string (or a type that can be explicitly converted), this throws an InvalidCastException. This behavior aligns with the “fail-fast” principle when the type must be a string for the subsequent logic to function correctly.

item.title: C Integer Division Producing Unexpected Float Results: Solutions Explained
item.description:
“C Integer Division Producing Unexpected Float Results: Solutions Explained”

A common perplexity in C arises when dividing two integer variables, where the result appears truncated, even when assigned to a float type. This behavior stems directly from C’s type promotion rules during arithmetic operations. When the division operator (/) operates on two integers, the operation is performed using integer arithmetic, producing an integer result by discarding any fractional part (truncation toward zero). This integer result is then implicitly converted to a float upon assignment, leading to seemingly incorrect decimal values.
